questions.stem: A 65-year-old P3L3 visits the clinic with complaints of feeling pressure in her pelvic region for the past three months. She also complains of a sensation of a bulge against her undergarments. There is significant past medical history suggestive of stage III endometrial carcinoma, now in remission, for which she received radiotherapy to her pelvis. She has 15 pack-year history of smoking. On further questioning, she described that at times she needs to use her finger to “push against the bulge” to achieve a bowel movement. On inspection, a mucosal outpouching is seen protruding from the vaginal opening. Upon transillumination of the protrusion, characteristic shadows were identified within the mucosal sac. On physical examination, the defect observed is most likely associated with the prolapse of the small bowel into the space normally occupied by the posterior vaginal wall between which pair of ligaments?
